result.markdown: --- title: "Take Home Exercise 1" author: "Gautamgovan" date: "September 13, 2025" date-modified: "last-modified" format: html: toc: true number-sections: true execute: eval: true echo: true warning: false freeze: true --- ## Overview This take-home exercise investigates the **spatial** (“where”) and **spatio-temporal** (“where + when”) patterns of **new business registrations in Singapore** between **1 Jan 2024 and 30 Jun 2025**. Using the ACRA “Information on Corporate Entities” datasets and SSIC 2020 classifications, we select at least **three business types** (2- or 3-digit SSIC) and analyse how their locations and intensities evolve over time. Our workflow mirrors the point-pattern framework taught in class: - **Data wrangling & geocoding:** tidy ACRA records, standardise dates/SSIC codes, and geocode by postal code via OneMap; convert to `sf` with SVY21 (EPSG:3414). - **Exploratory mapping:** counts by subzone/planning area to establish baseline patterns. - **First-order analysis (intensity):** **Kernel Density Estimation (KDE)** to reveal spatial hot spots for each SSIC and period. - **Second-order analysis (dependence):** **Ripley’s K / CSR envelopes** to test whether registrations are clustered, random, or dispersed. - **Spatio-temporal analysis:** **STKDE** (monthly slices) to detect **emerging, persistent, and fading** clusters over the study window. The results are communicated through cartographic maps and concise figure captions words , followed by a synthesis translating findings into **urban land-use and economic development implications**—e.g., infrastructure readiness, zoning flexibility, activation of under-served subzones, and monitoring of over-concentration risks. ## The Data This study uses ACRA corporate entity registrations combined with reference layers and services to enable spatial and spatio-temporal analysis. ### Data sources | Dataset Name | Description | Format | Provider | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---| | **ACRA – Information on Corporate Entities (A–Z, Others)** | All entity registrations. Used to extract new businesses by SSIC and date. | CSV (27 files) | data.gov.sg / ACRA | Split alphabetically: A–Z plus a 27th file for names starting with digits/symbols. | | **SSIC 2020** | Singapore Standard Industrial Classification; used to choose business types (2-/3-/5-digit). | CSV/XLSX | SingStat | We derive `ssic2`, `ssic3` and use `primary_ssic_code`. | | **OneMap Search API** | Geocoding service to convert postal codes to coordinates. | Web API | SLA / OneMap | Returns WGS84 (lat/lon). We transform to SVY21 (EPSG:3414). | | **Master Plan Subzones (MPSZ 2024)** | Administrative subzone polygons for aggregation and mapping. | GPKG/Shapefile | data.gov.sg / URA/SLA | Reprojected to SVY21 (EPSG:3414) for analysis. | ### Fields used (ACRA) | Field | Meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | `uen` | Unique Entity Number (entity identifier) | 201912345K | | `entity_name` | Registered business name | ABC PTE. LTD. | | `registration_incorporation_date` | Registration date (YYYY-MM-DD) | 2025-03-14 | | `primary_ssic_code` | Primary SSIC code (2/3/4/5-digit) | 56111 | | `postal_code` | Registered postal code (should be 6 digits) | 018989 | | `entity_type` / `status` | Type/status if required for filtering | LIVE COMPANY | > Additional columns may exist in different ACRA dumps; we standardise names with `janitor::clean_names()` and coalesce equivalent fields where needed. ### Study coverage - **Temporal window:** 1 Jan 2024 – 30 Jun 2025 (inclusive). - **Spatial extent:** Singapore national boundary; mapping/aggregation by **subzone** and **planning area**. - **Business scope:** At least **three** SSIC types (2- or 3-digit groups, or 5-digit subclasses), selected prior to analysis. ### Pre-processing & wrangling (summary) - Read and row-bind **all 27 ACRA CSVs**; add `source_file` for provenance. - Standardise fields: parse `registration_incorporation_date` as Date (UTC), derive `year`, `month`. - **Postal code hygiene:** keep digits only, left-pad to 6; drop non-6-digit values before geocoding. - **Deduplicate** by `uen` + `registration_incorporation_date` (if necessary). - Filter to the target SSIC code set and to the study window. - **Geocode** unique postal codes via OneMap; join `X`/`Y` back to ACRA records. - Convert to `sf` (WGS84) → transform to **SVY21 (EPSG:3414)** for distance-based methods. - Join subzone attributes; save intermediates as RDS for reproducibility. ### Data quality & limitations - **Geocoding precision:** Postal codes resolve to building/entrance centroids, not unit-level; some industrial sites share codes. - **Registration vs. operation:** Registration date ≠ opening date; counts reflect legal registrations. - **Address anomalies:** Legacy/PO box or malformed postcodes may not geocode; these are excluded. - **Classification drift:** SSIC codes can change over time; we use the recorded `primary_ssic_code` as-is. ### Coordinate reference systems (CRS) - **Input:** WGS84 (EPSG:4326) from OneMap. - **Analysis/Maps:** SVY21 / Singapore TM (EPSG:3414), metres, suitable for KDE and K-functions. ### Ethical/usage notes - ACRA data contains **entity names** (public corporate info), not personal data. - Results are aggregated for planning insights; avoid singling out individual firms. ## Load Packages Following code chunk is used to load neccessary packages ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pacman::p_load( tidyverse, # dplyr/readr/purrr/stringr sf, tmap, # geospatial + mapping httr, # OneMap API calls lubridate, # year(), month(), etc. spatstat, # KDE, K-function, CSR (monolithic ok) spNetwork, # network KDE (optional/bonus) sparr, # relative risk (optional/bonus) plotly, # interactive plots (optional) gtsummary, # summary tables dplyr, janitor, stringr ) ``` ::: ## Data Wrangling ### Preparing the Subzone Boundary (why & how) This chunk converts URA’s **Master Plan Subzone (No Sea)** GeoJSON into a clean, projected **GeoPackage** with consistent field names. We use it as: 1) the **analysis window** for point-pattern methods, and 2) the **join layer** to aggregate new businesses by subzone/planning area. Extract data for planning ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sz_raw_path <- "data/geospatial/MasterPlan2019SubzoneBoundaryNoSeaGEOJSON.geojson" subzones <- st_read(sz_raw_path, quiet = TRUE) %>% clean_names() %>% # lower_case_names st_make_valid() %>% # fix any tiny geometry issues st_transform(3414) # SVY21 metres (needed for KDE/K-functions) ``` ::: Standardise key attribute names ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Helper: extract a field value from the HTML in `description` extract_field <- function(html, key){ m <- str_match(html, paste0("", key, "\\s*([^<]*)")) val <- m[, 2] val <- ifelse(is.na(val) | val == "", NA_character_, str_squish(val)) return(val) } subzones_std <- subzones %>% mutate( SUBZONE_NO = as.integer(extract_field(description, "SUBZONE_NO")), SUBZONE_N = extract_field(description, "SUBZONE_N"), SUBZONE_C = extract_field(description, "SUBZONE_C"), CA_IND = extract_field(description, "CA_IND"), PLN_AREA_N = extract_field(description, "PLN_AREA_N"), PLN_AREA_C = extract_field(description, "PLN_AREA_C"), REGION_N = extract_field(description, "REGION_N"), REGION_C = extract_field(description, "REGION_C"), FMEL_UPD_D = extract_field(description, "FMEL_UPD_D") ) %>% select(SUBZONE_NO, SUBZONE_N, SUBZONE_C, CA_IND, PLN_AREA_N, PLN_AREA_C, REGION_N, REGION_C, FMEL_UPD_D, geometry) %>% st_make_valid() %>% st_transform(3414) # save a clean, fast-to-load copy st_write(subzones_std, "data/geospatial/mpsz_subzones_2019_nosea.gpkg", layer = "subzones", delete_dsn = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Deleting source `data/geospatial/mpsz_subzones_2019_nosea.gpkg' using driver `GPKG' Writing layer `subzones' to data source `data/geospatial/mpsz_subzones_2019_nosea.gpkg' using driver `GPKG' Writing 332 features with 9 fields and geometry type Unknown (any). ``` ::: :::
